B2b-09-starch-test-leaf-steps

Step-by-step diagram of the iodine test for starch in a leaf, in six numbered panels in two rows. 1: a leaf in a beaker of boiling water over a Bunsen flame. 2: the flame turned off. 3: the leaf in a boiling tube of ethanol standing in the beaker of hot water (water bath), the ethanol turning green. 4: the now pale leaf being dipped in a beaker of warm water. 5: the leaf spread flat on a white tile. 6: iodine solution being added with a dropper, the leaf turning blue-black.
B2b-01-chloroplast-internal-structure

A chloroplast in cut-away view, oval-shaped, showing the outer and inner membranes of the envelope, several stacks of disc-shaped thylakoids forming grana, thin intergranal lamellae linking the stacks, the stroma filling the space, two or three starch grains and a small ring of DNA. A small inset at the top left shows a palisade cell full of chloroplasts, with an arrow pointing to one chloroplast. Chloroplast in soft greens, stroma pale green, starch grains white.
B2b-02-photosynthesis-whole-plant

Diagram of a whole green plant showing the raw materials and products of photosynthesis. A sun at the top left sending rays to a leaf. Arrows: CO₂ from the air entering the leaf through stomata; oxygen leaving the leaf; water absorbed from the soil by root hairs, travelling up the stem in the xylem to the leaf (blue arrows); sugar travelling from the leaf in the phloem to the roots and to a fruit (orange arrows).
B2b-05-light-requirement-leaf-experiment

Three-step diagram of the experiment to show that light is necessary for photosynthesis. Step 1: a potted plant inside a dark cupboard, labelled destarching for 24–48 hours. Step 2: the same plant in sunlight with one leaf having a strip of aluminium foil clipped over the middle part on both sides. Step 3: the tested leaf on a white tile after the iodine test: the uncovered parts dark blue-black and the band that was covered brown. Optional fourth small panel: a leaf with a stencil showing the letter L in blue-black on a brown background.
B2b-06-carbon-dioxide-requirement-experiment

Side-by-side diagram of two bell-jar set-ups to show that carbon (IV) oxide is needed for photosynthesis. Set-up A (left): a destarched potted plant with a polythene bag tied over the pot, standing on a glass plate under a bell jar sealed with Vaseline at the rim; beside the pot, a small dish of potassium hydroxide solution. Set-up B, control (right): identical but with a small dish of water (or sodium hydrogen carbonate solution) instead. Sunlight shining on both. Beneath each jar, the tested leaf: brown for A, blue-black for B.
B2b-08-oxygen-production-photosynthesis-experiment

Apparatus to show that oxygen is produced in photosynthesis. A glass beaker of water containing shoots of pondweed under an inverted glass funnel raised on two small blocks; an inverted test tube full of water over the funnel stem, with gas collecting at the top; bubbles rising from the pondweed; a sun or lamp shining on the beaker from the side. A small inset shows a glowing splint relighting at the mouth of the test tube.
B2b-11-plant-mineral-deficiency-water

Water culture experiment. Four identical glass jars in a row, each wrapped in black paper with a clear window strip, each with a cork stopper holding a maize seedling with roots hanging in the solution and a thin glass tube for bubbling air. Jar 1 "complete solution": a tall, healthy, dark green plant. Jar 2 "no nitrogen": a short, thin plant with yellow lower leaves. Jar 3 "no phosphorus": a short plant with dark green leaves tinged purple and small roots. Jar 4 "no potassium": a plant with brown, scorched leaf edges on the older leaves.
B2b-12-leaf-nutrient-deficiency-symptoms

Three leaves side by side, plus one healthy leaf for comparison, all drawn as broad dicot leaves of the same shape. Healthy leaf: uniform dark green. Nitrogen deficiency: uniformly pale yellow-green leaf. Phosphorus deficiency: dark bluish-green leaf with purple-red tints along the edges and on the underside, and a purple-tinged leaf stalk. Potassium deficiency: green leaf with a yellow then brown, dry, scorched margin and tip, and a few brown spots near the edge. Below them, a second row showing three maize plants: N-deficient (small, with lower leaves yellow in a V-shape from the tip down the midrib), P-deficient (small, with purple leaf edges), K-deficient (brown scorched edges on lower leaves, stem bent over).
B2b-10-chemosynthesis-soil-bacteria

Diagram of chemosynthesis by nitrifying bacteria in the soil. A cross-section of soil with a decaying leaf and animal droppings at the surface releasing ammonia. Rod-shaped Nitrosomonas bacteria taking in ammonia and oxygen and releasing nitrite, with an energy symbol; then Nitrobacter bacteria taking in nitrite and oxygen and releasing nitrate, with an energy symbol; nitrate being absorbed by a plant root. A side box showing a single bacterium using the energy released to turn CO₂ and water into sugar.
B2b-04-photosynthesis-rate-line-graph

A line graph of the rate of photosynthesis (y-axis) against light intensity (x-axis). Three curves: the lowest curve levels off early; the middle curve levels off higher (high CO₂, 25 °C); the top curve levels off highest (high CO₂, 35 °C). On the lowest curve, mark the rising part as "light is the limiting factor" and the flat part as "another factor is limiting". Axis labels: rate of photosynthesis, light intensity. Simple coloured lines (green, blue, orange) with a small key.
